providers.service_territory: Portland metro area and surrounding communities including Hillsboro, Beaverton, Gresham, Lake Oswego, Tualatin, Salem area, and parts of the northern Willamette Valley
providers.notes: Largest IOU in Oregon. Delivers commercial efficiency programs through Energy Trust of Oregon (ETO), funded by a 3% public purpose charge per SB 1149. Schedules 32, 38, 83, 85, 89 are primary commercial tariffs.

providers.service_territory: Eastern Oregon, southern Oregon, and portions of the Willamette Valley including Medford, Bend, Klamath Falls, Pendleton, Albany, Corvallis, Lebanon, and surrounding rural areas
providers.notes: Second largest IOU in Oregon (dba PacifiCorp). Delivers commercial efficiency through Energy Trust of Oregon. Also maintains own Schedule 115/116 tariff-based incentive programs. Rate case effective January 2025 increased rates ~8.5%.

providers.service_territory: Customers of Portland General Electric and Pacific Power statewide (electric); also NW Natural, Cascade Natural Gas, and Avista (gas)
providers.notes: Independent nonprofit program administrator established 2002 per Oregon SB 1149. Funded by 3% public purpose surcharge on PGE and Pacific Power customers. Delivers prescriptive, custom, new construction, SEM, and agriculture programs on behalf of both IOUs.

providers.service_territory: City of Eugene and surrounding areas in Lane County
providers.notes: Largest municipal utility in Oregon. Offers prescriptive, custom, lighting, and solar rebates for commercial customers. Not served by Energy Trust of Oregon.

providers.service_territory: City of Springfield and portions of Lane County
providers.notes: Municipal utility serving Springfield, OR. Offers commercial energy efficiency rebates independently.

providers.service_territory: Portions of the Salem/Marion County area (co-op)
providers.notes: Consumer-owned cooperative. Offers residential, commercial, and industrial efficiency rebate programs. Also participates in EV charging rebates.

providers.service_territory: Central Oregon including portions of Deschutes, Crook, Jefferson, and Wheeler counties
providers.notes: Consumer-owned electric cooperative in central Oregon. Offers non-residential lighting rebates and EV charging incentives for commercial customers.

programs.stacking_rules: Can stack with federal tax credits (IRA); cannot stack with Pacific Power Schedule 115/116 for same measure
programs.program_notes_ai: Serves PGE and Pacific Power commercial customers. Covers lighting, HVAC, motors, VFDs, food service, compressed air, building controls, insulation, and water heaters. DLC required for lighting. Trade Ally network contractors are preferred but not mandatory. Funded by public purpose surcharge. Program administrator: Energy Trust of Oregon.

programs.stacking_rules: Can stack with SEM program; cannot stack with prescriptive incentive for same measure
programs.program_notes_ai: Requires pre-qualification of equipment and a funded Technical Analysis Study completed by an Allied Technical Assistance Contractor (ATAC). Post-installation verification may be required. Serves PGE and Pacific Power territory customers. Suitable for non-standard or complex efficiency measures not covered by prescriptive tables.

programs.stacking_rules: Can stack with federal tax incentives (179D, ITC); cannot double-count measures
programs.program_notes_ai: Cash incentives at every step of design and build process. Early design assistance meetings available. Contact team at newbuildings@energytrust.org or 1.877.467.0930. Serves PGE and Pacific Power territory. Multifamily new construction has a separate program pathway.

programs.stacking_rules: Can stack with prescriptive and custom incentives
programs.program_notes_ai: 12-15 month enrollment period. Cash incentives: $0.02/annual kWh saved (electric, PGE/Pacific Power territory). Milestone payments of $1,000 per milestone achieved. Intern support up to $10,000 for SEM-related intern (min 80 hours). Participants learn energy use patterns and identify waste. Call 1.866.605.1676.

programs.program_name: Industry & Agriculture – Prescriptive and Custom Incentives (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Can stack with federal incentives; cannot duplicate measure across prescriptive and custom pathways
programs.program_notes_ai: Includes standard incentives for lighting, motors, pumps, VFDs, compressed air, and custom incentives for process improvements. Industrial SEM program also available. Agriculture sub-program includes energy-efficient pumps, irrigation systems, and greenhouse equipment. Reported 19.2 aMW of Industrial and Agriculture sector savings in 2023.

programs.program_name: Schedule 115 – C&I Energy Efficiency Retrofit Incentives ≤20,000 sq ft (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Total incentives including BETC shall not exceed 100% of incremental cost of the EEM; minimum qualifying incentive total of $250
programs.program_notes_ai: Tariff-based prescriptive incentive program for C&I facilities 20,000 sq ft or less. Incentives shall not exceed 50% of incremental measure cost (except beverage vending machine occupancy sensors). Minimum qualifying incentive total of $250. Lighting interaction with mechanical equipment savings not eligible. Custom measures capped at 35% of Measure Funding Limit times annual energy savings or incremental cost, whichever is less.

programs.program_name: Schedule 116 – C&I Energy Efficiency Retrofit Incentives >20,000 sq ft (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Total Company-paid incentives shall not exceed 100% of incremental cost of the EEM; custom measures at 35% of lesser of Measure Funding Limit × savings or incremental cost
programs.program_notes_ai: Tariff-based program for C&I facilities larger than 20,000 sq ft. Custom measures require company analysis and sole discretion on incentive offer. EEM defined as permanently installed measure improving electric energy efficiency. Industrial facilities (manufacturing buildings and process equipment) are eligible. Lighting interaction with mechanical savings not eligible.

programs.stacking_rules: Partners with Energy Trust of Oregon and Connected Energy; stacking with ETO incentives may be available for qualifying measures
programs.program_notes_ai: Delivered in partnership with Energy Trust of Oregon and Connected Energy. Covers energy-efficient pumps, irrigation systems, greenhouses, and other agricultural equipment. Pacific Power has highly effective irrigation efficiency and demand response programs per ACEEE.

programs.program_name: EWEB Business Energy Efficiency – Prescriptive Rebates (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: EWEB is the largest municipal utility in Oregon. Offers rebates for fixture upgrades and technical assistance. Covers lighting (LED), HVAC, and other efficiency measures. Custom projects also available for measures that don't fit prescriptive program. Not served by Energy Trust of Oregon.

programs.program_name: EWEB Business Energy Efficiency – Custom Incentives (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: Contact EWEB directly to start conversation on custom projects. Offered for energy efficiency ideas that don't fit existing prescriptive programs or for carbon footprint reduction goals. Technical assistance provided.

programs.program_name: Salem Electric Commercial & Industrial Efficiency Rebate Program (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: Consumer-owned cooperative. Offers residential, commercial, and industrial rebates. Covers lighting, HVAC, and other efficiency equipment. Also participates in EV charging incentive programs.

Central Oregon consumer-owned cooperative. Primary commercial program is non-residential lighting retrofit rebates. Also offers EV charging rebates: up to $1,000 per commercial charging port and $150 per NEMA 14-50 outlet for commercial customers.

rate_schedules.notes: TOU option for small commercial. Peak/off-peak rates are approximate; verify against current PGE tariff. Updated Jan 1 2025.

rate_schedules.notes: Eligible for Direct Access and Daily Market Pricing elections. Rates approximate; verify against current PGE tariff. Updated Jan 1 2025.

rate_schedules.description: Above 4,000 kW demand; transmission/primary voltage; largest industrial and commercial customers
rate_schedules.notes: Eligible for Direct Access election. Rates approximate; verify against current PGE tariff. Updated Jan 1 2025.

rate_schedules.description: Street and area lighting services for municipalities and government customers; also Schedules 491, 495, 591, 595 for related lighting variants
rate_schedules.notes: Labor rate updated April 2025 per IBEW Local 125 collective bargaining agreement. Applies to municipalities and state/federal agencies with PGE crew luminaire replacements.

rate_schedules.notes: Rates approximate. Verify against current Oregon Price Summary PDF at pacificpower.net. Rate effective April 2026 Price Summary also available.

rate_schedules.notes: TOU option. Approximate January 2025 rates for secondary voltage per Pacific Power website. Verify against current Oregon Price Summary.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule 76 / 76R – Large General Service Partial Requirements
rate_schedules.description: Large general service partial requirements; includes Economic Replacement Power Rider and Delivery Service options
rate_schedules.notes: Schedule 76R is partial requirements delivery service variant. Rates approximate. Verify against current filed tariff.

rate_schedules.notes: Pacific Power has highly effective irrigation efficiency and demand response programs per ACEEE. Rates approximate; verify against current Oregon Price Summary.

rate_schedules.description: Small commercial service without demand metering
rate_schedules.notes: EWEB is a municipal utility; rates set by EWEB Board. Rates approximate; verify against current EWEB rate schedule.
Rates approximate; verify against current EWEB rate schedule.

rate_schedules.description: Large commercial and industrial customers with higher demand
rate_schedules.notes: Rates approximate; verify against current EWEB rate schedule.

forms.form_notes: Tariff schedule document includes incentive agreement terms. Applicants must execute an Energy Efficiency Incentive Agreement with Pacific Power as a condition of receiving incentives.

forms.form_notes: Application available via EWEB business rebates page. Contact EWEB directly for current form download links and program details.

forms.form_name: Energy Trust Commercial Incentive Application (PGE Territory)
forms.form_notes: PGE commercial customers apply through Energy Trust of Oregon. Same ETO application form used for PGE and Pacific Power territories. Customers must pay the public purpose surcharge to qualify.

forms.form_name: Energy Trust Commercial Incentive Application (Pacific Power Territory)
forms.form_notes: Pacific Power commercial customers apply through Energy Trust of Oregon. Customers must be served by Pacific Power and pay the public purpose surcharge. Same form used across both IOU territories.
